    Roots of weakly positive unit forms #

    Let q be a weakly positive unit form. A root is a nonzero r ≥ 0 with q(r) = 1, and ∂_i(r) = B(r, e_i).

    • partial_le_one, neg_one_le_partial: ∂_i(r) ∈ {-1, 0, 1} on the support.
    • exists_descent: a root above another root descends to it one coordinate at a time.
    • exists_minimal_pair: a root containing u ≠ j lies above a root s with s_u = s_j = 1, ∂_u(s) = ∂_j(s) = 1, and ∂_k(s) = 0 elsewhere on the support.
    • end_or_line (Lemma R): for a root z and c in its support, either z is a clean line starting at c, or there is a good end: w ≥ 0 with w_c = 2, q(w) ≤ 2, supported in z.
    • false_of_glue: two good ends at t with orthogonal rest contradict weak positivity.
